§ 02 The Feature

Three brothers, one kitchen.

Mohammad, Wassim and Omar Orfali, three brothers, Syrian roots, one kitchen. Their bistro at Wasl 51 in Jumeirah 1 is playful and story-driven: every plate carries a memory, a journey or a joke, and the menu refuses to sit inside any single cuisine. It is fine dining told the way a family tells stories at its own table.

That approach rewrote what fine dining in Dubai could be. The cooking is personal, and the rules of the tasting-menu format, hushed, formal, predictable, were left at the door. What arrived instead was a bistro that behaves like a storybook: course by course, plate by plate, entirely on the brothers' own terms.

The record followed the cooking. Orfali Bros sat at No.1 on MENA's 50 Best for three consecutive years, reached No.46 on The World's 50 Best, and in 2026 collected two Michelin stars, the full set of honours, earned by a restaurant that never once played by the book it was handed.

Three brothers. Two stars. Zero rules, not a slogan pasted on afterwards, but the order the story actually happened in.

Fine dining, minus the rules.
